subject: Post-call: LuminaHealth benchmark priorities & tokens/sec checklist
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: LuminaHealth benchmark priorities & tokens/sec checklist

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a proposed lightweight benchmark checklist so we can align on scope before we spin up infra.

Summary of asks from LuminaHealth during the call:
- Primary goal: choose an inference provider with predictable p95/p99 latency for interactive assistant flows and best cost per token for high-throughput batch scoring.
- Constraints: HIPAA-adjacent data handling, prefer VPC/private endpoints; sample traffic ~50k tokens/day per prod node for initial sizing.

Redwood proposed experiment matrix (MVP):
1) A/B: Redwood (v1.3 quantized) vs HyperscalerCorp managed endpoint (their default config).
2) Metrics to capture: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (server-side), tokens/sec (measured as decoded tokens/sec per-request and aggregate TPS tokens/sec), successful responses (%), and token billing delta.
3) Workloads:
   - Short chat: mean prompt+completion ~128 tokens (simulate 1.5K requests/hr)
   - Medium conversation: 512 tokens (simulate bursty sessions)
   - Long context probe: 2048 tokens (cold/warm cache)
4) Scenarios: cold start (new container), warm with KV cache, KV cache disabled, batching enabled (batch sizes 4/8), and quantization variants (int8 / fp16).
5) SLOs to validate: p95 < 250ms for short chat; p99 < 600ms desirable for our interactive path.
6) Duration & scale: 48-hour run with a controlled microburst window (5 minutes every hour at +3x traffic) to observe tail behavior.

Attachments: bench-config.yaml (initial infra settings), lumina_test_promptset.json (sample prompts). If you can share a sample of real-ish requests (anonymized) and the top 10 production prompt templates we should emulate, we'll tune the workload generator.

Open questions for you:
- Which hyperscaler endpoint(s) do you want included for head-to-head? (they mentioned two vendors on the call)
- Any procurement constraints / firewall IPs we should be aware of for private endpoints?
- Who on your ops team should receive the test run calendar invite?

Proposed kickoff slot: Wed Apr 14 morning PT — we can hand off to infra and run the 48-hour window starting Thu 03:00 PT.

If that aligns, we’ll provision test clusters (Redwood Dedicated sandbox) and share the data collection dashboard (p95/p99, tokens/sec charts) and a short readout doc at the end.

Thanks — Avery

--
Avery Johnson
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.com
(415) 555-0142

From: Samir Patel <samir@luminahealth.com>

Cc: eng-bg@luminahealth.com
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: LuminaHealth benchmark priorities & tokens/sec checklist

Avery — thanks for the clear recap and the checklist. This looks good and matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Hyperscaler endpoints: please include HyperscaleCorp (managed-public) and CloudPrime (their new managed API). We want both in the A/B matrix.
2) Data handling: sample requests will be PII-free, but we need the VPC option for production. For the bench runs you can use our anonymized dataset (I’ll share a link).
3) Ops contact: forwarding to eng-bg; they’ll coordinate IP whitelists.

Two asks: can you add a simple cost-per-token projection at the end of the run (raw token charges + estimated infra amortization) and a short section on fallback behavior (how Redwood degrades if a model variant is temporarily unavailable)? Those are key for our procurement folks.

We’re available to kick off Thu Apr 15 (rather than 14) — prefer a slightly later start.

Samir
VP Engineering, LuminaHealth
samir@luminahealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: LuminaHealth benchmark priorities & tokens/sec checklist

Samir — appreciate the quick reply and the hyperscaler targets. A few operational notes from our side before kickoff:

- Cost projection: we’ll output a per-run CSV that includes token usage, estimated infra minutes, GPU-hours, and an estimated $/1M tokens normalized for the configs we test (quantized vs fp16).
- Fallback behavior: Redwood’s routing layer will automatically redirect to a compatible model variant in the same region per policy; we’ll include the fallback matrix and a 0–100% degraded-latency simulation during the readout.
- Measurement: please confirm whether your SREs want server-side (provider) timings only or a combination with client-perceived latencies (we recommend both).
- Test data: Samir — please drop the anonymized sample and the top-10 prompt templates into the Drive link so we can seed the generator.

We’ll also test two quantization sweeps: int8 and 4-bit (where supported) and record accuracy regression metrics on your prompt set. For the microburst test, we’ll include 1-minute sustained peak at 5x baseline as an optional extra if you want stress validation.

Jonas — can you confirm infra provisioning ETA and the model versions we’ll pin for the initial run?

Thanks — Marissa
--
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions & Bench Ops, Redwood Inference
